children: The dollar may rise further against most currencies thanks to resilient U.S. growth and other tailwinds, strategists at OCBC Group Research say in a report. Other tailwinds consist of sticky U.S. inflation and growing Fed rate-hike expectations, the strategists say. "Fed rhetoric remains hawkish," the strategists say, citing overnight remarks from Fed officials such as St. Louis Fed President Musalem. "The upcoming FOMC minutes should provide more insight into how broad the hawkish shift has become," the strategists add. The U.S. dollar edges 0.1% higher to 1.2887 Singapore dollars and is 0.2% higher at 33.85 baht, but is little changed at 63.572 pesos, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
